report.summary: Cluster-wide CPU exhaustion is blocking the paymentservice rolling update. The scheduler cannot place the new pod (revision 7) because all 3 nodes report 'Insufficient cpu'. The old pod (revision 6) remains resident with 23 restarts and exit code 137 (SIGKILL), perpetuating resource contention. The rolling update is stuck indefinitely in a degraded state.
report.root_cause: All 3 cluster nodes have exhausted their allocatable CPU capacity. The paymentservice rolling update (triggered at 2026-08-19T06:51:49Z) cannot proceed because the scheduler cannot place the new pod revision 7 on any node. The old pod from revision 6 remains running but is trapped in a crash loop (23 restarts, exit code 137 indicating SIGKILL/resource pressure), preventing resource deallocation and exacerbating the CPU starvation.
evidence: Pod event FailedScheduling on paymentservice-695584ff5d-t8bhb (revision 7): '0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu. no new claims to deallocate, preemption: 0/3 nodes are available' — explicit scheduler CPU exhaustion message across all 3 nodes
New pod paymentservice-695584ff5d-t8bhb stuck Pending with node=null since 2026-08-19T07:25:25Z — cannot be placed on any node
Old pod paymentservice-798c77c577-g8gj6 has 23 restarts with exit_code=137 (SIGKILL) — indicates termination by signal due to resource pressure (OOMKill or kernel eviction)

Rollout timeline: revision 6 created 2026-08-03T05:31:13Z (pod began crashing immediately and continuously); revision 7 created 2026-08-19T06:51:49Z (triggered rolling update); new pod enters Pending at 2026-08-19T07:25:25Z with CPU exhaustion error
Old pod logs show normal transaction processing (no error output) — workload logic is sound, but process is being killed by kernel/scheduler due to resource pressure
Node status: all 3 nodes report Ready=True and MemoryPressure=False, but scheduler explicitly names CPU insufficiency — CPU is the sole constraint
alternatives: Other workloads in cluster consuming CPU (score 0.6): No evidence of competitor workloads; cluster-wide workload survey not performed — cannot rule in/out definitively

Deployment spec in revision 7 increased CPU request/limit (score 0.5): Rollout history shows identical image (v0.10.5) across revisions with no change_cause; scheduler reports absolute CPU unavailability ('Insufficient cpu'), not request mismatch

Old pod consuming excessive CPU causing starvation (score 0.4): MemoryPressure=False on all nodes rules out OOMKill as direct cause; pod logs show normal transaction processing rate, not pathological CPU use; explains mechanism but does not isolate root cause (could still be other workloads)
RollingUpdate strategy misconfigured (score 0.3): Scheduler explicitly reports CPU exhaustion, not strategy errors; identical images and no spec changes detected in rollout history

Node affinity/taints preventing scheduling (score 0.15): Scheduler message names 'Insufficient cpu', not affinity or taint violations; old pod successfully runs on k3d-sre-lab-server-0, proving no blocking taints
report.impact: paymentservice deployment is stuck in an incomplete rolling update state. New pod cannot start (Pending indefinitely). Old pod is crashing repeatedly (23 restarts) with increasingly severe restart backoff, risking complete failure. Service is running on an unstable, crashing pod, resulting in degraded availability and elevated risk of total service outage if restart backoff exhausts.

remediation.action: Undo the rolling update to remove the new (unschedulable) pod revision and pause scheduling attempts, allowing cluster CPU pressure to stabilize and enabling root-cause investigation of CPU consumption sources.
remediation.rationale: The new pod (revision 7) cannot schedule due to cluster CPU exhaustion. Undoing the rollout removes the new ReplicaSet and eliminates the scheduler's active attempts to place the new pod, reducing demand on an exhausted resource pool. This stabilizes the cluster and allows the old pod (revision 6) to run without concurrent scheduling pressure. The old pod remains in the crash loop, but the immediate blocking issue (pending pod + scheduler thrashing) is resolved. Long-term remediation requires identifying and addressing what is consuming cluster CPU: either reduce other workload resource consumption, add cluster capacity (nodes), or investigate a resource leak in paymentservice or its dependencies.

timeline.what: Revision 6 created (ReplicaSet paymentservice-798c77c577) with image v0.10.5; pod starts running
Pod from revision 6 begins crashing repeatedly; by investigation time it has 23 restarts with exit_code 137 (killed by signal, likely OOMKilled)
Revision 7 created (ReplicaSet paymentservice-695584ff5d) triggering rolling update with same image v0.10.5
New pod paymentservice-695584ff5d-t8bhb enters Pending; scheduler emits FailedScheduling warning: '0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu. no new claims to deallocate'
New pod remains Pending indefinitely; old pod continues running and crashing, holding CPU resources

correlation.what_changed: Rollout from revision 6 to revision 7 initiated at 2026-08-19T06:51:49Z; new pod cannot schedule because all 3 nodes report insufficient CPU, and the old pod (23 restarts, exit code 137) remains resident and unable to release resources
correlation.summary: Cluster-wide CPU exhaustion is blocking the new pod's scheduling. The old pod is stuck in a crash loop (exit code 137 indicates termination by signal, likely OOMKilled) and continues to consume resources. No image change between revisions, no cascading downstream failure—the incident is a resource contention issue at the cluster level.

hypotheses.cause: All cluster nodes have exhausted their allocatable CPU capacity; the scheduler cannot place the new pod (revision 7) on any node
supporting: Pod event FailedScheduling: '0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient cpu. no new claims to deallocate, preemption: 0/3 nodes are available'
New pod paymentservice-695584ff5d-t8bhb remains Pending with node=null
Old pod paymentservice-798c77c577-g8gj6 has 23 restarts with exit_code=137 (SIGKILL), suggesting resource pressure forcing eviction
against: Insufficient direct observability: no CPU usage metrics from query_prometheus or detailed node resource breakdown provided
MemoryPressure=False on all 3 nodes, ruling out memory as the bottleneck (though CPU exhaustion can coexist with false MemoryPressure if kernel hasn't yet updated the condition)

hypotheses.cause: Other workloads in the cluster (outside the boutique namespace) are consuming CPU, leaving insufficient capacity for paymentservice rollout; paymentservice deployment is competing for shared cluster resources
supporting: Scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient cpu' on all nodes, consistent with cluster-wide resource pressure
Evidence is scoped only to boutique namespace; cluster-wide workload consumption was not queried
Rolling update strategy requires capacity for (old + new) pod concurrently, which will fail if cluster is near 100% utilization
against: No evidence collected about other namespaces or workloads — cannot confirm competitor workloads exist or their resource footprint
get_workload_status was called only for boutique namespace with app=paymentservice selector; a cluster-wide survey would be needed to rule this in or out definitively

hypotheses.cause: Deployment spec in revision 7 increased the new pod's CPU request/limit beyond cluster available capacity, while revision 6 (old pod) specified lower requests and was already running; rolling update strategy cannot evict old pod fast enough to make room
supporting: Timing: new pod created at 2026-08-19T06:51:49Z cannot schedule while old pod still running
Both pods use identical image tag, but ReplicaSets could specify different resource requests — this would explain why old pod runs but new pod cannot
Rolling update strategy: new pod waits for old pod to terminate, but old pod cannot be terminated if CPU is already exhausted
against: No evidence of spec change in rollout_history output — both revisions use identical image, and no change_cause field indicates resource request modification
Scheduler message names absolute CPU unavailability ('Insufficient cpu'), not request mismatch; if new pod's request was simply too high, scheduler would show 'Insufficient resources for X cpu'
If this were the root cause, we would need to inspect the actual Deployment manifest to confirm resource request differences — tool output does not show this

hypotheses.cause: Old pod (revision 6) is consuming excessive CPU (potential runaway or CPU leak), starving the cluster and blocking the new pod from scheduling; exit code 137 (SIGKILL) suggests OOMKill or resource pressure killing, not clean shutdown
supporting: Old pod has restart_count=23, exit_code=137 (SIGKILL), indicating repeated forceful termination consistent with resource exhaustion
Old pod is actively processing transactions (logs show PaymentService#Charge invocations), proving it is running and consuming CPU
If old pod is in a loop (legitimate activity or bug), it could fully saturate cluster CPU, leaving zero capacity for new pod
against: Node status shows MemoryPressure=False on all nodes; if the old pod were OOMKilled, we would expect at least one node to report MemoryPressure=True
No evidence of CPU spike in the old pod's logs — transaction processing logs look normal, not pathological (no fast restart cycle visible)
Exit code 137 could also result from a manual termination during rollout, not necessarily from resource pressure
This hypothesis explains a mechanism but does not rule out the real cause being broader cluster saturation from other workloads

hypotheses.cause: Deployment rolling update strategy (RollingUpdate) is incorrectly configured or a rollout is in a degraded state, preventing successful pod scheduling and old pod eviction
supporting: Rollout is in progress: progressing=true, unavailable=1 (new pod Pending)
Old pod has high restart count, suggesting the update process is not proceeding cleanly
against: This is a symptom, not a root cause: the scheduler's explicit message is 'Insufficient cpu', not a RollingUpdate configuration error
Both old and new pods use identical image (v0.10.5), so no image change is driving the update
Rollout history shows only image identity across revisions; no evidence of spec changes that would trigger or misconfig the update strategy
A RollingUpdate issue would manifest as maxUnavailable/maxSurge misconfiguration or strategy errors, not scheduler CPU exhaustion

hypotheses.cause: Node affinity, taints, or pod scheduling constraints (nodeSelector, nodeAffinity, tolerations) in the new pod spec prevent scheduling on the only available nodes, or a new taint was added to all nodes after the old pod started
supporting: Could theoretically restrict a pod to nodes that are full or unavailable
against: Scheduler event explicitly names 'Insufficient cpu', not affinity or taint violations; scheduler would report 'node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' if this were the cause
Old pod is successfully running on k3d-sre-lab-server-0, proving at least that node is usable and not tainted in a way that blocks paymentservice
No evidence of node taints or affinity constraints in tool output; get_node_status showed no taint conditions
